edits.find:
Three fractures are abuse until proven otherwise in a young child: a metaphyseal corner (bucket-handle) fracture, which needs a forcible pull or twist of the limb; a posterior rib fracture, from squeezing the chest; and a femur fracture in a child who does not yet walk. The bone-disease mimics each need their own finding on the film or exam: osteopenia with cupped, frayed metaphyses for rickets; blue sclerae and many low-energy fractures for osteogenesis imperfecta; a punched-out lytic lesion for Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

A risk factor in the history (breastfeeding without vitamin D, no prenatal care, a parent's single childhood fracture) is not that finding; a film with normal bone density and a classic abuse fracture answers it.

edits.find:
Fever, a petechial rash and shock in a preschooler is septic shock, and septic shock is by definition distributive: inflammatory mediators produce vasodilation and capillary leak, so blood is maldistributed rather than absent, inadequate or obstructed.

The trap is that she does not look vasodilated. Capillary refill of 4 seconds is cold shock, which is how children usually present — they compensate by vasoconstricting and running the heart rate up, so the bedside picture mimics hypovolemia. Note also what the stem withholds: there is no blood pressure, because in children hypotension is a late, pre-arrest finding.

edits.find:
Nothing is wrong with this infant, so the question is sequence. At 6 months she has crossed the gate for complementary foods, and she has crossed it correctly — iron-fortified cereal is already in the diet, which is the first complementary food because iron is the limiting nutrient once fetal stores deplete at 4 to 6 months.

Having started with an iron source, the next move is variety: pureed vegetables and fruit, one new single-ingredient food at a time. Every other option is the right intervention at the wrong age — finger foods belong at 8 to 9 months, whole milk at 12 months, and exclusive breastfeeding through 6 months and not beyond.
